Chapter 9: Handling Criticism and Navigating External Doubt
As you make progress on any meaningful path, you’ll probably run into a little criticism—or even some outright skepticism—from the people around you. Maybe it comes from friends, family, or coworkers who genuinely care but just don’t quite get what you’re trying to do. Sometimes, they’ll question your choices or worry about your decisions. Other times, they might flat-out tell you your new venture sounds risky.
So, how do you handle all that external doubt and keep moving forward? Well, it all starts with recognizing that this is a skill—one that helps you stay true to yourself even when others don’t see your vision yet.
Let’s be honest, criticism can really sting, especially if it comes from people you respect or love. Here’s something to pay attention to: not all criticism is created equal. There’s a big difference between constructive feedback and just plain negativity.
Constructive feedback actually has your best interests at heart. It’s pretty specific and usually comes from someone who wants to see you improve. On the flip side, unhelpful criticism tends to be vague, dismissive, or even rooted in other people’s own fears—not yours.
Think of criticism like the weather. Some days are sunny and you feel supported. Other days, well, you might face a downpour of doubt or disapproval. The trick? Carry your own internal umbrella—a sense of self-belief and some healthy boundaries to keep you steady, no matter the forecast.
Here are a few ways you can navigate criticism and external doubt without losing your momentum:
First, listen for value. Is there something in the feedback that could actually help you grow? If so, take it on board. If not, just let it go.
Next, set boundaries. If someone keeps bringing negativity into your life—especially if they aren’t really on board with your goals—it’s okay to limit how much time and energy you give them.
And don’t forget to strengthen your “why.” Remind yourself why you made these choices in the first place. When your purpose is clear, it’s a lot easier to weather those storms of doubt from the outside.
Here’s another thing to remember: everyone sees the world through their own unique lens. What feels risky or strange to one person might seem totally normal—or even exciting—to someone else. Trusting your own judgment, while staying open to learning, is a balancing act, but it’s so important.
Want a real-world example? Think about inventors whose ideas were laughed at, only to be celebrated later for their creativity. Or artists who got criticized for their unique style, but eventually found an audience who loved what they did. The common thread is simple—they kept going, even when others didn’t understand or approve.
So, here’s the key takeaway: handling criticism isn’t about ignoring everyone or shutting out feedback. It’s about focusing on what matters most to you. By filtering what you hear and staying true to your own values, you’ll find the confidence and resilience you need to keep pushing forward—no matter what kind of weather comes your way.
